events.title: Sounds of South Asia Musical Performance

cases.refreshed: As a kickoff to the 'Sounds of South Asia' exhibit, students of Indian and Nepali origin in the Bay Area will perform on the sitar, sarod, sarangi, and madal, stringed and percussion instruments of South Asian music, and will be accompanied by an adult musician on the tabla, another percussion instrument. All these instruments have long traditions in India, Nepal, and other South Asian countries. In the diaspora, the children continue these traditions by continuing to learn and perform. If you are new to South Asian music or if you are familiar, join us to celebrate South Asian culture by hearing some instruments performed live and then see the new exhibit of 'Sounds of South Asia' that just opened at the library. Come and explore the exhibit by using the QR code to listen to the sounds of the instruments displayed in the exhibit. Program is for children 5 and up and family members interested in South Asian music.

events.title: Sounds of South Asia: an exhibit

cases.refreshed: This interactive photography exhibit showcases several musical instruments from the South Asian subcontinent. Each exhibit will have a QR code that allows participants to listen to the sound of the instruments performed in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. They include stringed, wind, and percussion instruments passed down from generations, which are still performed around the Bay Area. Come and enjoy this exhibit which starts on November 14, 2026, closing on December 5, 2026. The exhibit is brought to you by the South Asians in Silicon Valley initiative at the SJSU King Library. Through this unique initiative, the SJSU King Library records, preserves, and shares the living legacy of the South Asian diaspora in the San Francisco Bay Area. Website: https://library.sjsu.edu/sasv
